key_insight: Remanent strain fields and line-like defects created by plastic compression in magnetite do not measurably shift or broaden the Verwey transition, unlike point defects.
engineering_relevance: For solid mechanics and damage engineering, the study shows that extended slip-related defects can be mechanically significant yet electronically benign compared with point-like disorder.
method: Dark-field x-ray microscopy (DFXM) to image defect structures, lattice orientation, and residual strain
Ac magnetic susceptibility to track the Verwey transition temperature and sharpness
Compare stoichiometric single-crystal magnetite after compression, unloading, and fracture under different loading axes
evidence_signal: Across compressed and fractured samples, DFXM revealed substantial remanent disorder, but susceptibility measurements showed no measurable change in Verwey transition temperature or transition sharpness.
watch_item: The conclusion is specific to stoichiometric single-crystal magnetite under the tested loading paths, so it should not be generalized to other materials, defect types, or stress states without verification.
paper_title: Robustness of the Verwey transition against remanent strain-induced defects in magnetite
